title: President approves 78 Gallantry awards (13 posthumous) & 89 Mention-in-Despatches on the eve of 80th Independence Day
body_text:
President Smt Droupadi Murmu has approved 78 Gallantry awards, including 13 posthumous, to the personnel of the Defence Forces and Central Armed Police Forces on the eve of Independence Day 2026. These are: 09 Kirti Chakras including 07 posthumous; 01 Bar to Shaurya Chakra; 19 Shaurya Chakras, including 01 posthumous; 05 Bar to Sena Medals (Gallantry); 36 Sena Medals (Gallantry), including 05 posthumous; 03 Nao Sena Medal (Gallantry); and 05 Vayu Sena Medals (Gallantry). enrichment.summary: President Droupadi Murmu approved 78 Gallantry awards (13 posthumous) and 89 Mention-in-Despatches for Defence Forces and Central Armed Police Forces personnel on the eve of the 80th Independence Day, 2026. The gallantry awards comprise 9 Kirti Chakras, 1 Bar to Shaurya Chakra, 19 Shaurya Chakras, 5 Bars to Sena Medal (Gallantry), 36 Sena Medals (Gallantry), 3 Nao Sena Medals (Gallantry) and 5 Vayu Sena Medals (Gallantry). The Mention-in-Despatches went to 75 Army, 4 Navy and 10 Air Force personnel for various counter-insurgency and security operations including Operation Rakshak, Hifazat, Orchid, Meghdoot and Snow Leopard.
enrichment.context:
India's peacetime gallantry awards are announced twice a year, on Republic Day and Independence Day, recognising acts of bravery by armed forces and central armed police personnel in operations against insurgents, terrorists, and along disputed borders. The awards follow a fixed order of precedence: Ashoka Chakra (highest, equivalent to Param Vir Chakra for non-battlefield gallantry), followed by Kirti Chakra and Shaurya Chakra, with corresponding service-specific medals (Sena, Nao Sena, Vayu Sena Medals) for lower-tier recognition. Mention-in-Despatches is a distinct, lesser honour denoting gallant or distinguished service mentioned in official military dispatches.

This year's list reflects continuing operations in Jammu & Kashmir (including J&K Police personnel honoured for Operation Rakshak-related counter-terror actions) and in the Northeast (Assam Rifles personnel decorated for operations like Hifazat, Orchid, Meghdoot, Snow Leopard, and others named after specific counter-insurgency operations). Such announcements are largely ceremonial and administrative in nature, honouring individual and unit valour rather than announcing any new policy, scheme, or institutional change, and are published annually without altering the broader gallantry award framework.
